# 19 — Frontier Capstones

This is a synthesis chapter, not a source of new machinery.  Read Chapters
14–18 first, then attempt a problem before reopening the relevant chapter.  A
capstone is successful when you can explain the reduction in ordinary words:
what an algebraic coefficient represents, why the operation preserves that
meaning, and why every division or randomized step is legal.

Allow 3–5 team-hours per problem.  Before coding, write a one-page proposal:
the algebraic object, its coefficient domain, the invariant or theorem that
connects it to the statement, target complexity, and any randomized error
bound.  This turns “try a transform” into a testable model.

## Problems and learning route

1. **[make 1 — ABC278 Ex](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc278/tasks/abc278_h).** Model rank growth of vectors over $\mathbb F_2$ and recognize a Gaussian binomial count.
   <details><summary>After an honest attempt</summary>Review [Gaussian binomials](../14-modular-combinatorics/chapter.qmd#gaussian-binomial-coefficients): the key object is a subspace, not a collection of independent coordinates.</details>
2. **[Long Binary String — CF1698G](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1698/G).** Translate repeated shifts into multiplication in $\mathbb F_2[x]$ and use factor information.
   <details><summary>After an honest attempt</summary>Review [finite-field factorization](../15-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd#degree-decomposition). State exactly which quotient ring represents the allowed operations.</details>
3. **[Lights Out on Connected Graph — ARC105 F](https://atcoder.jp/contests/arc105/tasks/arc105_f?lang=en).** Count all labelled objects first, then extract the connected contribution.
   <details><summary>After an honest attempt</summary>Review [set-series exp/log](../16-set-power-series/chapter.qmd#functions-of-a-set-series). Identify the unique connected-component partition before applying a logarithm.</details>
4. **[Degree Harmony — ABC412 G](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc412/tasks/abc412_g?lang=en).** Turn a constrained matching question into the lowest nonzero term of a determinant polynomial.
   <details><summary>After an honest attempt</summary>Review [Tutte matrices](../17-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd#tutte-matrix) and write the Schwartz--Zippel degree bound for the exact polynomial you evaluate.</details>
5. **[Chinese Elephant Chess — QOJ 60](https://qoj.ac/problem/60).** Compress a labelled component model to a differential equation and a P-recurrence.
   <details><summary>After an honest attempt</summary>Review [the series/sequence bridge](../18-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd#translation-between-series-and-sequences). A recurrence is useful only after its initial values and singular indices are specified.</details>
6. **[Graphs — QOJ 11139](https://qoj.ac/problem/11139).** Replace a formidable multiple sum with a certified polynomial-coefficient recurrence.
   <details><summary>After an honest attempt</summary>Review [guessing and certification](../18-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd#guessing-and-fast-evaluation). Empirical agreement supplies a conjecture, not the final proof.</details>

## Postmortem template

For each problem, record the recognition clue, algebraic model, preconditions,
target complexity, randomized error bound if any, and the smallest brute-force
oracle that could have caught the first bug.  Also write one sentence naming the
first tempting but wrong tool—for example, ordinary subset convolution when
labels may overlap, or factorial division when a denominator is a non-unit.
